comment: The five clocks and eight effects are not placed by hand: each object owns two rolled positions and the two morph knobs glide the whole population between them, which is the one deliberate departure from the original's mouse canvas. Divisions and effect kinds never change, only positions. The field display is a custom widget rather than a control, so no click in it reaches this help; a muted player is drawn there as a hollow ring rather than a filled dot. Mute, volume and the engine switch are all exempt from Rack's randomize and from the module's own randomize button, because they are performance state rather than sound design. Loop windows drunk-walk in steps of 200ms up to the maximum loop length, and samples come from a bank of 64 by an urn, so the same one never comes twice in a row. The module is inspired by Giorgio Sancristoforo's Haiku: the architecture, timing model, effect designs and voice behaviour follow a reverse-engineering of it, while the generator's numbers were tuned by ear. The sylla module plays the same generated library as a standalone voice. The panel prints imber, x, y, chg, new, clk, fx, rch, cpl, cv, bpm, spd, lpm, skp, sks, scv, rvl, vol, rnd, pls, inst, plv, div, bit, nse, tap, on, seed, rr clk, nd clk, rr fx, nd fx, trg, clr, xcv, ycv, 2n, 4n, 8n, 16n, 32n, skip, micro, L and R.
